title: Two Treatises of Government
description: John Locke, 1689. Against absolute monarchy; government rests on the consent of the governed and exists to protect natural rights.

title: Discourse on the Origin of Inequality
description: Jean-Jacques Rousseau, 1755. The state of nature, the invention of property and the social origin of inequality among people.

title: The Social Contract
description: Jean-Jacques Rousseau, 1762. The general will, the sovereign people, liberty as obedience to a law citizens give themselves.

title: Leviathan
description: Thomas Hobbes, 1651. The state of nature as a war of all against all and the covenant that sets up a sovereign.

title: Perpetual Peace
description: Immanuel Kant, 1795. Republican constitutions, a federation of free states and a cosmopolitan right as the conditions of lasting peace.

title: On Liberty
description: John Stuart Mill, 1859. The harm principle: society may limit a person's liberty only to prevent harm to others. Liberty of thought and discussion.
